title: Court Turmoil
next_chapter_hook: Chen Ji received an anonymous secret letter at the Crown Prince's birthday banquet, containing only four words — "The chess game is not yet finished"

text.content:
Imperial City. Crown Prince's Birthday Banquet.

The vermilion palace walls glistened with a blood-red sheen under the setting sun, three hundred and sixty glazed palace lanterns illuminating the courtyard of Taihe Hall as bright as day. High officials, sect elders, and martial heroes gathered together, and beneath the toast and cups, hidden currents surged.

Chen Ji stood at the end of the guest queue, dressed in unassuming cyan robes with jade belt, wearing a dark-colored small cap, looking no different from an ordinary disciple some minor sect had sent to make up the numbers. He lowered his gaze and restrained his presence, taking in everything around him — including the Crown Prince on the high seat inside the hall with his false smiles and pleasantries, and Su Qingyao in the corner, whose eyes constantly cast searching glances.

That jade pendant inscribed with his birth date and eight characters — where did it come from?

Three days ago, he was still sitting in contemplation at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain when he received an invitation with no signature — golden-edged cloud-patterned letter paper, with dragon's saliva fragrance hidden within the inner layer of the luxurious paper. Only imperial dedicated materials could possess such quality.

He did not ask about its origin.

Only that person could have him infiltrate the banquet under the identity of "Heavenly Secrets Pavilion Hidden Agent." Chen Ji touched the fragment inside his sleeve — Master Mo had manifested late last night, leaving only one sentence: "This banquet is perilous, yet it is your optimal timing to enter the game."

Master Mo never spoke idly. Peril meant variables; entering the game meant opportunity.

dialogue.content: (Thought) That jade pendant in Su Qingyao's hand... if it truly is Eldest Brother's relic, the scheme behind this is likely far deeper than I anticipated.

text.content:
Just then, the music inside the hall suddenly changed.

The Crown Prince rose and personally raised his wine cup, proclaiming loudly: "Distinguished guests, today I am honored by Father's graciousness to host this banquet, deeply grateful for everyone's support of the royal family over these many years. I have an announcement to make —"

He paused, his gaze sweeping across everyone present, finally landing on a large object covered with red silk in the center of the hall.

"Father has granted me permission to travel to the Imperial Mausoleum for ancestral worship next month, where I shall open the Dragon Vein Altar that has been sealed for a hundred years, to pray for the Yan Kingdom's enduring fortune!"

The hall erupted in an uproar. The Dragon Vein Altar — that was an Ancient Forbidden Land rumored to be bound to the Yan Kingdom's national fate!

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly.

The Dragon Vein Altar. He had seen this name in the fragments Master Mo had deciphered — it was a forbidden ground where countless living beings were sacrificed to seal an ancient existence. During the war among the three kingdoms a hundred years ago, the Yan ancestors had used its power to repel foreign enemies, but at a devastating cost.

Opening the altar? Praying for the nation's fortune?

Chen Ji's gaze turned cold. Either the Crown Prince had lost his mind, or someone was using this opportunity for unspeakable purposes. He下意识 turned his gaze toward Su Qingyao — the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow was staring fixedly at the object beneath the red silk, her brow furrowed tightly.

What had she sensed?

dialogue.content: (Thinking privately) Interesting... this chess game probably has more than one player.

choice.prompt: Before the Crown Prince had even finished speaking, the hall was already filled with heated discussions. You decide —

choices.description: During the gift-offering segment, deliberately approach the mysterious object, using the Tianji Record Fragment to sense any hidden energy within, confirming whether it is an ancient seal.
choices.risk_hint: High risk — if detected, will expose your identity

text.content:
Chen Ji借口更衣, quietly circling toward the side of the hall. The fragment in his sleeve grew slightly warm — that was the reaction only when the Tianji Record sensed a major turning point. When he approached within three zhang of the object, the fragment suddenly turned ice-cold.

The seal... was loosening.

He only glimpsed a corner, yet was already horrified — beneath that red silk was clearly the core of a Soul Refining Formation using living humans as sacrifices!

dialogue.content: (Inhaling sharply) What ambition... they want to use the Dragon Vein's power to resurrect something?

choices.description: Resist the urge to act, continue maintaining your "waste" persona, observe the reactions of various forces, waiting for clearer geopolitical patterns to emerge.

text.content:
Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, lifting his wine cup to take a small sip, as if he were just some闲人来蹭吃蹭喝的. But his divine sense always enveloped the entire hall, not missing any trace of abnormality.

As expected — when the Crown Prince made this announcement, one person's expression changed in the corner. From the Xuanwu Sect direction, a sturdy young man's eyes flashed with a barely perceptible gleam of ecstasy.

Han Lie.

dialogue.content: (Thought) Interesting... the Xuanwu Sect is so interested in the Dragon Vein matter... could they also be eyeing this altar?

choices.text: Induce others to take the lead
choices.description: Secretly pass hints to Su Qingyao, using her hand to expose part of the truth, while keeping yourself uninvolved to reap the fisherman's advantage.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing the connection with Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: Act without entangling karma, using others as the blade
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao might follow the trail and uncover your background

text.content:
Chen Ji flicked his finger gently, and a silent sound-transmitting talisman flew through the air, landing precisely by Su Qingyao's ear.

'Beneath the red silk, a living sacrifice. If Senior Sister Su has doubts, you may examine the formation patterns at the altar's base—that is an ancient evil formation using blood as its guide.'

Su Qingyao's body stiffened, instinctively turning to look in Chen Ji's direction. But he had already averted his gaze, casually savoring the pastries before him.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao: Who are you? How do you know such things in this setting?

text.content:
Just as undercurrents swirled in all directions, a commotion suddenly arose outside the hall.

A black-robed guard rushed in and knelt, reporting: 'Your Highness, an elderly visitor seeks an audience, claiming to be... the Tianqing Sect's Master, Ling Yuan!'

Chen Ji's fingers holding the wine cup tightened imperceptibly.

Ling Yuan? What business brought him here? More crucially—why would someone supposedly in seclusion at Tianqing Sect suddenly appear at a palace longevity banquet?

dialogue.content: Ling Yuan (stepping into the hall, with white hair yet youthful features, an immortal demeanor): This old one was in seclusion at the Rear Mountain when I sensed the unusual dragon energy emanating from the imperial capital. I came to investigate. Please forgive my abruptness, Your Highness.

text.content:
The prince's expression flickered briefly before returning to normal. He smiled and said, 'Master Ling is highly respected. Your presence is my honor. Someone, offer a seat!'

Yet Ling Yuan showed no haste to sit, instead slowly surveying everyone in the hall. When that profound gaze like a deep abyss swept past Chen Ji, he felt a chill run down his spine—as if some primordial beast had locked its eyes on him.

At that moment, he nearly believed himself discovered.

Yet Ling Yuan merely glanced at him dismissively before turning away, as if Chen Ji were truly just an insignificant nobody.

But Chen Ji noticed the old man's fingers gently rubbing a jade pendant in his sleeve—and its quality and size were remarkably similar to the one Su Qingyao held.

A matching pair.

These two jade pendants were originally one set.

dialogue.content: (Internally alarm bells ringing) Ling Yuan... just how many trump cards are you still hiding?

text.content:
The longevity banquet continued, with songs and dance masking the lurking killing intent beneath.

Chen Ji quietly retreated to the corridor beside the hall, intending to find an opportunity to investigate the red-silk-covered object. Yet an unexpected figure blocked his path.

Han Lie.

The number one prodigy of Xuanwu Sect stood with arms crossed, looking down at him from above, a contemptuous smile playing at the corner of his mouth: 'Oh, isn't this the famous waste servant from Tianqing Sect? When did someone like you get into a palace longevity banquet?'

dialogue.content: Han Lie: What, lost your tongue? Speak up, waste! Last time at the ruins you barely escaped with your life. This time you won't be so lucky. If you know what's good for you, scurry back to Tianqing Sect and scrub toilets!

choice.prompt: Han Lie provokes you publicly. You decide—

choices.description: Dismantle him with words, reducing him to nothing, letting everyone present see exactly how ugly this Xuanwu prodigy's true colors are.
choices.visible_reward: Gain public fame by defeating Han Lie
choices.risk_hint: Expose your edge, drawing Ling Yuan's attention

text.content:
Chen Ji leisurely set his wine cup on the corridor pillar, raising his head with an amused smile: 'Young Master Han, such a fiery temper. Could it be that Xuanwu Sect's salary isn't enough, so you're here in the imperial capital to collect debts?'

Nearby, someone couldn't help but chuckle. Han Lie's expression darkened, about to lose his temper, when Chen Ji unhurriedly continued: 'Ah yes, about the ruins incident... I still remember Young Master Han kneeling on the ground begging for mercy. Quite a spectacular sight.'

dialogue.content: What, need me to help Young Master Han reminisce? After all, that scene... isn't something just anyone gets to witness.

choices.text: Playing the pig to eat the tiger
choices.description: Appear panicked and beg for mercy on the surface, but actually provoke the conflict, causing Han Lie public humiliation, laying the groundwork for subsequent schemes.
choices.visible_reward: Han Lie relaxes his guard while secretly laying plans
choices.risk_hint: Need to endure for a moment, waiting for the right moment to counterattack

text.content:
Chen Ji seemed frozen in fear, quickly bowing in salutation: "Young Master Han, please calm your anger. I merely came on orders to offer birthday congratulations, with absolutely no intention of offense..."

As he spoke, he "carelessly" took a step backward, and a talisman in his sleeve quietly activated. Han Lie was about to reach out and shove him, but his fingertips touched an invisible barrier, followed by a foul stench emanating from his body—a sinister technique that catalyzed human stench tenfold!

The surrounding guests scrambled to cover their noses, whispering amongst themselves.

dialogue.content: (Cold smile in heart) Han Lie, Han Lie, you think I'm on the first level, but I'm actually on the fifth level.

choices.description: Too lazy to waste time on insignificant clowns, turn around and continue with the original plan, gathering more intelligence about the Dragon Vein Altar.
choices.visible_cost: Give up the chance to publicly defeat Han Lie
choices.visible_reward: Preserve energy for more important matters
choices.risk_hint: Might be seen as weak and easy to bully by Han Lie

text.content:
Chen Ji couldn't even be bothered to glance at him, merely saying calmly: "If Young Master Han is bored, perhaps he should ask His Highness the Crown Prince—has your sect ever made a move for what's beneath that red silk?"

With that, he walked away with hands clasped behind his back, leaving a stunned Han Lie standing frozen in place.

These words seemed casual, yet precisely struck at the vitals of certain people.

dialogue.content: (Thinking to himself) Insignificant clowns, not worth mentioning. I have more important matters to attend to.

text.content:
Chen Ji moved between the grand halls, evading squads of patrolling guards, approaching the massive object covered in red silk.

However, just as he was about to reach his target, an aged voice rang out behind him: "Young friend, this place is not where you should be."

Chen Ji's footsteps faltered. He slowly turned around.

Ling Yuan had somehow appeared ten paces behind him. Moonlight cast an eerie pallor over that crane-white hair and child-like face. The old man smiled, but his eyes held absolutely no warmth.

dialogue.content: Ling Yuan: OldLing Yuan observed that your face seems unfamiliar. Which sect's outstanding disciple might you be? How does a servant from the Tianqing Sect gain access to the imperial capital?

text.content:
Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression remained calm as he bowed respectfully: "The junior is indeed of servant origins from Tianqing Sect, but a noble benefactor bestowed favor upon me, granting an invitation to broaden my horizons. If there was any offense, I hope the senior will understand."

Ling Yuan narrowed his eyes, his gaze growing increasingly profound: "A benefactor? Which noble person possesses such means?"

Chen Ji raised his head, meeting those eyes that seemed capable of seeing through everything, word by word: "Does the senior truly wish to know?"

dialogue.content:
Ling Yuan (frowning slightly): What do you mean by those words?

Chen Ji (slight smile): The junior merely wishes to say—some matters, knowing too much, is not necessarily a blessing. Wouldn't the senior agree?

choice.prompt: Ling Yuan pressing relentlessly, the situation reaches a critical juncture. You decide—

choices.text: Reveal your trump card to intimidate
choices.description: Intimate that you are aware of the connection between Ling Yuan and those jade pendants, as well as the grudge between him and Chen Xuan, forcing the other party to hold back due to投鼠忌器 concerns.
choices.visible_reward: Intimidate the old fox, gain breathing room
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan might attack on the spot

text.content:
Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back, his voice extremely low: "The jade pendant in the senior's sleeve, isn't it a matching pair with the one in Senior Sister Su's possession? The junior dares to guess—that is Fellow Apprentice Chen Xuan's legacy."

Ling Yuan's pupils contracted sharply, his surrounding aura suddenly surging, pressing down on Chen Ji until he could barely breathe.

"You—" The old man's voice trembled, "Who exactly are you?"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji (facing that terrifying pressure, grinning): Why must the senior be so agitated? The junior is merely a chess piece trying to survive. As for the senior... how many years has this chess game been going on? Are you tired?"

choices.text: Pretend to be foolish to escape
choices.description: Go along with the previous "benefactor's favor" story, fabricate a backer, feint and escape, avoiding direct conflict with this old fox.
choices.visible_reward: Escape safely, preserve your trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan might be secretly investigating your background

text.content: Chen Ji hastily waved his hand, wearing an expression of being overwhelmed: "Senior is mistaken, how would I dare have any trump cards? I'm merely a servant running errands for that noble person. If Senior wishes to know that noble person's identity, I could help introduce you—though, of course, this will have to wait until after the birthday banquet." Ling Yuan narrowed his eyes to examine him for a moment, but ultimately did not make a scene on the spot: "...Forget it. The old man remembers today's matter."

dialogue.content: (Cold smile in his heart) Old fox, trying to extract information from me? Come back in a few more decades.

choices.description: Secretly trigger the mechanisms set up beforehand, create chaos to slip away, and simultaneously expose Ling Yuan under the spotlight.
choices.visible_reward: Take advantage of the chaos to escape, leaving Ling Yuan in a passive position
choices.risk_hint: May be drawn into a bigger storm

text.content: Chen Ji's fingertips moved subtly, sending a hidden Spiritual Energy fluctuation toward the distance. A moment later, a tragic scream suddenly echoed from somewhere within the hall, followed by billowing smoke! "Assassins—!" The hall erupted in chaos as the guards drew their blades and rushed toward the source of the sound. Ling Yuan frowned, instinctively looking back. In that split-second, Chen Ji had vanished like a ghost into the night.

dialogue.content: (Thinking while escaping) Ling Yuan, you thought you'd cornered me? Today, this game ends in a draw between us.

text.content: Chen Ji took advantage of the chaos to slip away, but he didn't go far. He circled to a secluded corridor behind the Taihe Hall, leaning against a vermillion column, his chest rising and falling slightly. The information tonight was overwhelming. Dragon vein altar, ancient seal, the Jade Pendant in Ling Yuan's hand, Han Lie's unusual reaction, Su Qingyao's other piece... all clues pointed to one possibility: this so-called prince's birthday banquet was merely the opening act of a much larger game.

And he was nothing more than a chess piece pushed into the game by fate. Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly echoed in his mind, aged and ethereal: "Boy, do you think you're the chess player?" Chen Ji smiled bitterly: "Master, please advise." "Under that dragon vein altar lies sealed a remnant soul of the ancient beast Zhuyin. Someone wants to awaken it, and the Tianji Record... is one of the keys." Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply.

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng: This old man can only tell you this much. How you proceed from here depends on yourself. However... remember, the bigger the chess game, the more the pieces' fates are beyond their control. If you wish to break this destiny, you must only—go further than the manipulators.

text.content: As his voice faded, Mo Xiansheng's presence completely dissipated. Chen Ji stood alone in the corridor, the night wind brushing past, ruffling his robes. Go further than the manipulators... He softly repeated these words, his eyes gleaming with brilliance. A moment later, he took out a blank Talisman Paper from his sleeve, used his finger as a pen, swiftly wrote a line of characters, folded it into a paper crane, and let it fly toward the direction outside the imperial city. That was his secret letter to Ye Qing—the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path should enter the game too.

Just as he prepared to leave, a soft footstep sounded from behind. Chen Ji turned sharply to find an unexpected figure standing under the moonlight—Su Qingyao. She held the Jade Pendant inscribed with Chen Ji's birth date in her hand, her eyes showing complex, indecipherable emotions: "I've been looking for you all night. So this is where you were hiding." Chen Ji narrowed his eyes and said nothing. Su Qingyao stepped closer, holding the Jade Pendant before him: "This... belonged to your eldest brother, didn't it? Tell me, who exactly are you?"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji looked at that Jade Pendant and suddenly smiled: "Senior Sister Su, some things become dangerous once known. Are you certain... you want to wade into these troubled waters?"

text.content: The night wind suddenly ceased. The commotion from the Taihe Hall direction continued, but this corridor had become terrifyingly silent. Chen Ji and Su Qingyao faced each other, the moonlight stretching their shadows long. Just as the atmosphere was about to freeze into ice, Su Qingyao suddenly spoke: "Ling Yuan approached you just now." This was not a question, but a statement. Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "Senior Sister Su's intelligence network is quite efficient." Su Qingyao snorted coldly: "That old fox harbors no good intentions. If you don't want to die不明不白, you'd better—" She paused, seemingly weighing her words, "let me know what you're investigating."

Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then suddenly extended his hand: "Let me see the Jade Pendant." Su Qingyao hesitated for an instant before handing over the Jade Pendant. Chen Ji received it and examined it carefully—the back of the Jade Pendant indeed bore a line of tiny seal script: "Heavenly Secrets turn, destinies intertwine." This was... the inscription of the Tianji Record. His heart stirred, and he unconsciously activated the fragment in his sleeve. In an instant, a profound fluctuation surged from the Jade Pendant, resonating with the fragment! "So that's how it is..." Chen Ji murmured, "This is the source of the fated twins."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao: Fated twins? What are you talking about? Chen Ji returned the Jade Pendant to her, his gaze deep: "Senior Sister Su, where did you obtain this thing? Tell me the truth."

text.content: Su Qingyao remained silent for a moment before finally speaking: "Before the birthday banquet began, I was resting in the side hall. A person in black quietly entered and slipped this Jade Pendant into my hand, then vanished. I didn't even see his face clearly." "What did that person say?" "Only one sentence—" Su Qingyao slowly said, "'Give this to Chen Ji, and he will understand.'" Chen Ji's eyes sharpened. Someone was secretly helping him, yet deliberately pushing him into a deeper whirlpool. Was this layout related to Mo Xiansheng? Or was it someone else entirely?

Just as his thoughts were in turmoil, a lantern suddenly lit up at the end of the corridor. A young eunuch hurried over and bowed: "Excuse me, are you Chen Ji Chen Gongzi? The Crown Prince requests your presence." Chen Ji and Su Qingyao exchanged glances, both seeing wariness in each other's eyes. The Crown Prince? Why would he summon an unknown nobody at this time? Chen Ji took a deep breath and straightened his clothes: "Please lead the way,公公." In the moment he turned, he suddenly felt something extra in his sleeve—a secret letter that had been slipped in at some unknown time.

Chen Ji did not immediately examine the letter, only firmly gripping it in his palm. Under the young eunuch's guidance, he passed through重重殿宇 and arrived at a secluded side hall behind the Taihe Hall. Sandalwood incense burned within the hall, and the Crown Prince stood with hands behind his back, facing away from the entrance. "You are Chen Ji?" The Crown Prince did not look back, his voicecalm得听不出情绪: "A servant disciple from the Tianqing Sect... no, perhaps I should call you—the inheritor of the Tianji Record?" Chen Ji's heart shook violently, but his expression remained unmoved: "Your Highness jests. I am merely atrash, how would I dare沾边 such a divine object as the Tianji Record."

dialogue.content: The Crown Prince slowly turned around, his pair of狭长的眼眸 flickering with playful light: "trash? A person who can make Ling Yuan personally come to test... this prince has never seen such atrash." He strode forward, looking down at Chen Ji: "I don't care who you are or what purpose you have. I only ask you one thing—" "Regarding the dragon vein altar, will you help this prince, or... help those who wish to awaken the beast?"

text.content: Chen Ji faced那双scrutinizing的目光 and suddenly smiled. "Your Highness, I am merely a小人物 who wants to survive. Such major matters... how would I dare get involved?" The Crown Prince narrowed his eyes, seemingly辨别 his words真假. After a long while, he waved his hand: "Forget it, you may leave. Tonight's matter, this prince will consider as if you never came." Chen Ji bowed in salute and turned to leave. Only after exiting the side hall did he discover his back was soaked with cold sweat. The Crown Prince was more formidable than he had imagined—this person clearly already knew his identity, yet chose to敲打 rather than揭穿, showing深不可测的心机.

Night had deepened, and the birthday banquet gradually dispersed. Chen Ji mingled with the guests heading toward the palace gate, and when no one was paying attention, he quietly unfolded the secret letter in his sleeve. Under the moonlight, only four ink characters appeared on the paper— "Chess game unfinished." The handwriting was achingly familiar. That was... Chen Xuan's handwriting. Chen Ji's fingers trembling as he held the letter. Eldest brother... you're still alive? What's going on with all this?!

The night wind of the imperial capital remained cold, yet it could not disperse the layers of fog shrouding Chen Ji's heart.

Dragon Vein Altar, ancient seals, twin fates of destiny, Ling Yuan's ambitions, the prince's probing, and that letter from a dead man... All the clues intertwined, weaving into a net whose full scope he could not yet perceive.

He believed himself to be the chess player, only to discover the chessboard had already been laid out.

He thought he was arranging the pieces, yet he was unaware that he might merely be a pawn being pushed within a far grander game.

But it didn't matter.

Chen Ji tucked the letter into his robe, a cold light suddenly flashing in his eyes—if he had already entered the game, then he would overturn this chessboard...!
